wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough measure of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, and one that rises when Iran is at the centre of an unfolding story rather than a background one.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership tracked a war restarting: US strikes resumed on 1 September after a month-long pause, and Iran answered the same night with missiles at Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan, where US troops are hosted. A strike on a wedding near Kuhestak killed five, a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent rose 3% to $90.97.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: War in the Gulf set the range. Brent peaked at $105.30 on Jul 23, and the Strait of Hormuz closed after two tankers were attacked; a supertanker then hit mines there, and US drones struck two Iranian oil tankers under a tanker-for-tanker policy. At $96.02 the barrel is well above July's $68.53 low, and Fed hike odds have jumped to two-in-three.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet US crude, the benchmark for oil produced and refined in North America. It is priced inland at a Oklahoma pipeline hub, so it tracks US supply and refining demand more closely than seaborne grades do.
wti.recent: US drones struck at least two Iranian oil tankers under a tanker-for-a-tanker policy, and prices jumped 4% on supply fears as fighting revived Middle East disruption risk. Washington's move on Venezuelan reserves added a second supply story. Fed hike odds rose to two-in-three as the shock fed through.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline junction in Louisiana and quoted per million British thermal units. It prices American power generation, heating and fertiliser feedstock, and anchors what US LNG cargoes cost abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The US benchmark has drifted down about 5% over two months, to $2.90 from a $3.34 high on Jun 30 and off a $2.56 low on Aug 7 — a domestic market decoupled from the squeeze abroad. European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on Sept 2, a three-year high, with EU storage near 64% and Delhi raising compressed natural gas ₹3.89 a kg as LNG spot prices surged.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. Harvests, export bans and the cost of fertiliser and freight set it, and bread prices and food-aid budgets follow.
wheat.recent: Wheat is a fifth more expensive than it was a year ago, at $228.7 a tonne in July 2026 against a low of $155.1 in September 2025. The input does not explain the rise, though the squeeze it puts on food budgets is visible: the World Food Programme is halving its West Bank operation and cutting support for 400,000 people, and Pakistan's food imports rose 8.12pc to $805.5m in July.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple calorie for more than half the planet and the grain most exposed to export bans. A handful of Asian shippers set the price, and import-dependent countries in West Africa and the Gulf pay it.
rice.recent: The series has fallen 16% over the window, to $464 a tonne, well off the $555 peak of Sep 2024 and closer to the Oct 2025 low of $330.6. Nothing in the material explains the decline.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in every grid, motor and building. Demand for it rises with wiring, so its price tracks how fast the world is electrifying — and how tight mine supply is against that.
copper.recent: Copper has climbed roughly 46% over the series, to $13,540/mt from a December 2024 low of $8,910, peaking in June 2026. The demand side is visible in the wiring itself: transformer designs are being reinvented for AI load, EV charging is straining grid voltage, and Washington has banned foreign grid parts. Mining pollution in Lualaba, DRC marks the supply end.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself over a decade. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate credit and emerging-market borrowing costs, so it is the rate almost every other rate is quoted against.
us-10y.recent: The move is an oil shock arriving as an inflation shock: Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes pushed the market from expecting a Fed cut to pricing a possible hike, and bonds were sold rather than bought. The yield reached 4.79% on Sep 1, with thirty-year yields at 5.3%, a 2007 level, and long-end term premium doing the work rather than the policy rate.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US-listed companies, and the default benchmark for American equities. Pension funds, index trackers and retirement accounts worldwide are priced against it.
sp500.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range after a run led by AI capital spending, with Nvidia pledging $500 billion to its own buyers and lending against GPUs entering the market. The drag now comes from rates: global bond yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears in early September.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. It is weighted toward technology, so a handful of chipmakers, platforms and software firms move it, and it is the usual proxy for how the sector is being valued.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its 62-day range after a run of company news: a judge in Alexandria ruled Google will not have to sell its ad exchange, rejecting the divestiture the Justice Department asked for and imposing behavioural remedies instead. Nvidia paid $3.5 billion in bonds for a stake option in MediaTek, and Apple handed the CEO job to John Ternus.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It tracks crude oil with a lag, but refining capacity, taxes and seasonal blending rules set how much of a crude move actually reaches the forecourt.
us-gas-retail.recent: The pump price eased to $4.071, down from the $4.146 high on Jun 8, well above the $3.777 low on Jul 6. Refining, not crude supply, is where the strain sits: Ukraine's drones struck the Samara refinery, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved" as Russia moved to import fuel and lower its standards.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered into the Dutch TTF hub, Europe's benchmark for wholesale gas. It sets what utilities pay to heat homes and run industry, and because Europe now buys much of its gas as seaborne LNG, it competes directly with Asian buyers.
natgas-ttf.recent: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, a three-year high, as EU storage sat near 64% ahead of winter and US-Iran hostilities pushed LNG buyers into competition for the same spot cargoes. Europe buys almost no Iranian gas — the move is displacement, not lost supply. Delhi's CNG price rose ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on the same LNG squeeze.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of market fear.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down roughly a quarter over the three months to 1 September, from 22.22 on 10 June to a low of 14.25 on 14 August and 16.34 now. Nothing in the record explains the decline beyond its own steadiness.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and much of its food, so the rate sets domestic prices, and it is the number the IMF, the Gulf depositors and remittance-sending families all watch.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee held in a narrow band, easing to 277 from a 278.8 high on Aug 31 — a move of a fraction of a percent across the month. Nothing in the period explains it: fuel taxes, floods in Islamabad and the Foreign Office's mediation between Washington and Tehran ran alongside a rate that barely shifted.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency against the dollar, the price at which Africa's largest economy trades oil earnings for imports. It carries the country's fuel, food and drug bills, and a weaker naira shows up first at the petrol pump.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to 1,328 from its Aug 8 high of 1,365 as foreign reserves hit a 20-year high and Moody's scored Abuja's austerity. FTSE Russell will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21, restoring frontier status and the index flows that follow it.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar, quoted as pounds per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker pound. It sets the cost of the wheat, fuel and fertiliser Egypt imports, and the burden of its dollar debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound slid to 51.06 after the US cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system on 28 August, part of a Treasury push that also targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties. Cairo has been courting alternatives: Xi Jinping arrived for his first state visit in a decade, urging a Middle East security order less dependent on Washington.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the cost of Turkey's imported energy and dollar debt, and it is the price most Turkish households read inflation through.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh 30-day low of 48.31 on Sep 3, about 1.6% weaker over the month, with no single break in the slide. The month's news around Turkey was diplomatic and maritime rather than monetary: Erdogan's SCO push, which he said does not mean abandoning the West, the first committee meeting of the Mecca defence pact in Istanbul, and a cargo collision off Silivri that left ten crew missing.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka, quoted per US dollar. Bangladesh runs on imported fuel, food and industrial inputs while earning dollars from garment exports and worker remittances, so the rate sets both factory margins and the price of a household's rice and cooking oil.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed slightly over the month, from 124 on Aug 7 to 122.4 now, a move of under one percent that is unremarkable against a currency this heavily managed. The month's political news out of Dhaka — a confirmed order for China's J-10CE fighters, a tribunal putting journalists on trial — left no visible mark on the rate.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar. Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest economy and a major commodity exporter, so the rate carries the price of its coal, nickel and palm oil into world markets.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah firmed across the month, from 17,940 on Aug 5 to 17,650 on Aug 21 before settling near 17,680. Nothing in the month's Indonesian news — Prabowo's tightening state grip on the economy, the captive coal powering the nickel boom, VTB's launch of QR payments in Indonesia — explains a move this small.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. After the collapse that wiped out most of its value, the peg is what Lebanese salaries, savings and imported food and fuel are priced through.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been close to flat for a month, moving less than a percent between its low on Aug 8 and its high on Aug 31, while Israeli attacks pushed Lebanon's death toll to 4,350 and troops occupied Christian villages near the border. The rate held through it.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's currency and the US dollar, managed within a band the People's Bank of China sets each morning rather than floated freely. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, so it moves trade balances everywhere.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to its strongest level of the month, 6.718, after a run of firmer domestic data: China's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August, and carbon emissions fell 1% on falling oil demand rather than a slowdown. Xi Jinping spent the week in Cairo pitching a Middle East security framework.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. It sets the cost of India's imported oil, fertiliser and electronics, and the value of the remittances its diaspora sends home.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed through late August and into September, reaching its strongest level of the month on Sep 3 after India's economy grew 7.8% in the June quarter. New Delhi then revised last year's economic base down by 7%, so part of that headline strength is arithmetic rather than output.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate between Brazil's real and the US dollar. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore, oil and coffee, so the rate sets what those cargoes earn at home and what dollar-priced debt and imports cost Brazilians.
fx-brl.recent: The real firmed about 1% over the month, easing from 5.222 on Aug 15 toward 5.093, with the wider low of 5.085 set on Aug 10. The fraud probe that brought down Bank Master kept domestic financial supervision in question through late August, and a new poll showed Brazil's socialist president losing his lead.

fx-mxn.standing: The Mexican peso's exchange rate against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. It moves on US trade policy, interest-rate gaps and remittance flows, and it prices the cost of Mexico's dollar-denominated trade.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened about 1.6 percent over the month, from 17.24 on Aug 6 to 16.92 on Aug 21 before settling at 16.98. The coverage window carries no Mexico-specific policy or trade development that accounts for the move.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, quoted here inverted as euros per dollar. It is the most traded currency pair in the world, and the rate at which the euro area's trade, debt and reserves are priced against the dollar.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted through a narrow band while Europe absorbed a run of security shocks rather than monetary ones: Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone attack and is closing Russia's consulate in Bonn, and two German substations were hit with homemade explosives. None of it moved the currency far — the range held inside a cent.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. It is the world's main funding currency, and it moves on the gap between Japanese and US interest rates.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar on 31 August as the rate gap widened: thirty-year Treasury yields reached 5.3%, a 2007 level, and Fed hike odds jumped to two-in-three this week. US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates, and traders in Tokyo moved to intervention watch.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker ruble. It carries the price of sanctions, oil receipts and capital flight into the cost of everything Russia imports.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid to 87.3 from 80.63 on Aug 5 as Russia's confrontation with Europe hardened: Germany formally blamed Russia for the attempted drone strike on an An-124 at Leipzig airport, the EU summoned Moscow's envoy and Germany moved to close the Bonn consulate. At home, 4.2 trillion rubles are shifting into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate between South Africa's rand and the US dollar. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and because South Africa imports its fuel and prices its mining exports in dollars, the rate feeds straight into what households pay at the pump.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed to 16.05 over the month, off its 16.36 low on Aug 7 and near the 15.92 high of Aug 26. The gain did not reach the forecourt: petrol rose R1.34 a litre on Tuesday, as the fuel formula passed through costs the stronger currency was expected to offset.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock and held now by funds, corporate treasuries and exchange-traded products. Its price is a gauge of appetite for risk and of demand for an asset outside any central bank's control.
btc.recent: The climb from the Aug 17 low was a short squeeze rather than fresh leverage: bearish bets lost a record $3 billion as Bitcoin broke a six-week range, and the run to $80,020 on Aug 28 came as traders priced Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. Basis-trade desks taking no view on price earned most.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement token of a network that hosts most stablecoins, lending protocols and token issuance. Its price is a proxy for demand to use that network, not just to hold the coin.
eth.recent: The rise came with a short squeeze rather than a single catalyst: bearish crypto bets lost a record $3 billion on 20 August as bitcoin broke a six-week range toward $71,000, and one trader who had made $49 million shorting lost $24 million on ether in 12 seconds. The peak on Aug 22 came at the end of that week.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a physical gold bar, so its price tracks an ounce of bullion while trading around the clock on crypto venues. It draws buyers when currencies, central banks or governments look unreliable.
paxg.recent: Gold ran up to $4,672 on 25 Aug as traders positioned around Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and the question of Fed independence, then eased back. The metal's role as an outside-the-system store of value showed elsewhere too: Islamic State buried $47 million in gold and cash at Deir ez-Zor, and Kassala street dealers outbid Sudan's licensed market.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article on the field of building machines that perform tasks associated with human reasoning. Its readership works as a rough gauge of how much public attention the technology commands on any given day.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership ran high in late August around a run of institutional collisions: a US court ruled the Pentagon's ban of Anthropic unlawful, Debian's developers voted to permit rather than ban generative AI in its packages, and the EU brought ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under its 'very large platform' rules.

wiki-russia.standing: The daily count of readers opening Wikipedia's article on Russia — the largest country on earth by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, and a major exporter of oil, gas, grain and fertiliser. Attention here tracks crises.
wiki-russia.recent: Germany formally accused Russia of an attempted drone strike on a Ukrainian An-124 cargo aircraft at Leipzig Airport, and the EU summoned Russia's envoy; Germany is closing Russia's consulate in Bonn, and Moscow summoned the German chargé d'affaires. Separately, Putin met Modi and Xi, and Siluanov returned to the G20 as European finance ministers boycotted the family photo.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up on any given day, which rises when it enters a story bigger than its own borders.

wiki-china.standing: Wikipedia's China article is one of the most-read country pages on the site, and daily readership on it tends to move when the country does something the rest of the world has to react to — a deal, a deployment, a policy shift.
wiki-china.recent: Readership tracked a run of Chinese activity abroad: Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo after a decade and urged Middle East states to reshape their own security order, Bangladesh confirmed a deal for China's J-10CE jets, and Vietnam demanded China halt construction on two Paracel features. Flash floods that closed Nepal's China trade corridor killed more than 1,000.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The 21-mile sea lane between Iran and Oman, and the only way out of the Persian Gulf. Around a fifth of the world's oil is loaded onto ships that must pass through it, so anything that narrows it is felt in every fuel market.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the closure: Iran declared that transit through Hormuz required Tehran's permission, then a supertanker hit mines in the strait and two tankers were attacked leaving it, stranding 6,000 sailors aboard anchored ships. US strikes on Larak Island and Iranian missiles on US bases in Jordan widened the exchange; Brent rose to $90.97.

wiki-india.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on India each day. It rises when the country is in the news, and the shape of the curve marks which days a story broke rather than what the story was.
wiki-india.recent: Readership peaked on Sep 1 around Modi's SCO summit meetings in Bishkek, where he held bilateral talks with Putin and Pezeshkian and urged peace in Ukraine while India remained Russia's second-largest oil buyer. The same window carried India's June-quarter GDP growth of 7.8% and the revision of the prior-year base from Rs 86.05 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.

wiki-ukraine.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on Ukraine. Attention to a country tends to move with events rather than with the country itself, so the series works as a rough register of when the war forces its way back into general view.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came amid the run of strikes that followed: a Russian attack on an arms depot near Kyiv where stored shells detonated and killed 37, and the loss of off-site power at Zaporizhzhia, which ran on diesel alone for a week. Attention has since fallen back toward the early-August low.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed as the US-Iran war reached the water: two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz, a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines in the strait, and Tehran now says transit requires its permission. US drones have struck Iranian oil tankers under a tanker-for-tanker policy. Brent rose 3% to $90.97.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Transits are running about a fifth below their 90-day baseline after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, the same week Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Razih district in Saada. Owners are pricing war risk rather than distance, and the low of 14 vessels came on 5 August.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic has recovered through the summer, from 22 vessels a day in mid-June to 57 on 11 August and 53 now — running above its own 90-day baseline. Attacks on shipping have not stopped: the Houthis said they struck a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August, and Pakistani nationals injured in a Red Sea attack returned home in late August.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic ran about 8 percent below its 90-day baseline, easing from the 27 July peak of 269 vessels a day. Warship movement is part of the picture — USS Abraham Lincoln crossed the strait after 285 days deployed — while tanker owners weigh a widening campaign against shipping, with two Iranian oil tankers struck by US drones and a Houthi missile hitting a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic over the past week ran about a seventh below its own 90-day baseline, in a period of sharpening friction around the island: Taipei disclosed six years of investigations into undeclared Chinese chip labs recruiting its engineers, and Hanoi demanded China halt construction on two Paracel features. Waves peaked at a mild 2 metres.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transit slots are being rationed rather than filled: the Panama Canal moved to cap daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño, and the 87-day range runs from 83 vessels on Jul 13 down to 23 on Jun 13. A separate dispute over canal ports has CK Hutchison seeking HK$11.7b from Panama.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen through a summer of incidents in and around the strait: two vessels collided off Silivri in the Sea of Marmara on 2 September, leaving ten crew missing, and a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus days earlier. Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships in the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near the middle of its range, roughly 3% below the 90-day baseline, with no weather to explain the dip. The disruption around the strait has been on land and in policy rather than at sea: Italy extended its Schengen suspension with Spain to September 15, and more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July, the Spanish enclave on the Moroccan coast a short distance east of the strait.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has held close to its own baseline, running about 1.2 percent below the 90-day average with wave heights peaking near 1.9 metres — no closure, no weather alert. The spread between the 1 August high of 186 vessels and the 3 August low of 126 is ordinary daily variation rather than a disruption.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has swung between 69 vessels a day on Jul 4 and 123 on Jul 31, and now sits within a tenth of a percent of its 90-day baseline. Seas are rough, with waves to 3.9 m. Red Sea risk keeps ships on this route: a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker at Yanbu on 24 August.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to nothing: the count first hit zero on Jul 17 after a high of 23 vessels a day on Jun 19, and the last week sits 100 percent below its own 90-day baseline. The wider war offers no shortage of pressure — Russian strikes, EU retaliation over the Leipzig drone attack — but nothing in the record names the cause of the shutdown itself.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its range, some 2.7% below where it stood a month ago, after a high of 11150 on Jun 16. Riyadh spent the period signing a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey in Mecca, whose first committee met in Istanbul, and negotiating a nuclear deal with Washington; neither explains the drift.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has drifted lower over the window, hitting 14,830 on Jun 18 and bottoming at 13,290 on Jul 30, and closed at 14,050 after a 1.3% fall. Ankara's positioning dominated the period: Erdogan pushed for SCO membership while denying a turn from NATO, and the Mecca defence pact's first committee met in Istanbul.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after a run of Gulf security shocks: the UAE downed an Iranian drone over its territorial waters on 31 August, following the missile attack that led Abu Dhabi to suspend all trade with Iran. Bessent has also targeted UAE banks over Iran ties.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after climbing from 1,657 on Jul 1 to a high of 1,749 on Aug 26. The one political shock in the window came the following day, when prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing some $40 million in assets — a case that touched him rather than any listed company, and the market barely moved on it.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The climb since June has run alongside a widening state hand in the economy: Prabowo's cooperatives programme has put the president's imprint across the economy, while the captive coal plants powering Morowali's nickel boom keep the export complex expanding. Foreign capital, though, stays scarce — RCEP has stabilised trade in goods without integrating capital.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index is down about a twentieth over the window, from its late-June high to a 29 July low. The yen fell past 160 per dollar, and US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates; Fed hike odds jumped to two-in-three this week as global bond yields hit multi-decade highs.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted down over the window from its 21 August high of 26,010, with the listings pipeline the clearest local signal: Shein's Hong Kong debut priced the fast-fashion group at $26.3bn, a discounted valuation for a venue of last resort. Beijing's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August, while Washington used the G20 to rally other economies against China's surplus.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits below its June high, with China's factory gauge rising to 51.5 in August on AI-related capex that has split Asian manufacturing rather than lifted it broadly. Washington is meanwhile rallying G20 states behind tariffs aimed at China's surplus, and Shein's lacklustre debut underlined weakness in the consumer export model.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00% on 27 August, a consecutive increase made in the name of financial stability, and the index sits well below its June high after a slide through late July. Lee Hyoung-il's promotion to finance minister set the policy pairing alongside it.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range after a run of domestic demand data: Honda's two-wheeler sales rose 8% to 579,000 units in August. New Delhi also cut last year's GDP base by 7%, which raises reported growth without adding output — the headline figure foreign funds price off is now measured against a smaller denominator.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth from its June low to a series high, with the run coinciding with Singapore's deepening trade position — Taiwan has become its largest trading partner — and a payments boom in which crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion. The feed window offers no single event behind the latest move.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index has clawed back most of a slide to 39,930 on Jul 30, helped by Nvidia's $3.5 billion convertible stake option in MediaTek on Sep 1, which sent MediaTek shares up 10%. The pull the other way is legal and political: Taiwan indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager over AI server smuggling.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index fell about 3.5% in a day to 1,581, near the bottom of a range that has held between 1,541 in late June and 1,639 in mid-July. Nothing in the available reporting on Thailand explains the drop.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the middle of its range for the period, well below the 6,404 high on Jul 17 and above the 5,879 low on Jun 8, after a sharp single-day drop. Nothing in the available material accounts for the fall.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index slid on 1 September after a Trump vow rattled trade-exposed sectors, and the domestic backdrop is weak: home prices fell for a fifth straight month, with homebuyer numbers collapsing and a rate war looming. KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff in the same window.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has held near the top of its range, closing at 115,100 after a peak of 118,200 on Aug 28 and a low of 108,300 on Jul 23. Nothing in the local record explains the move: the domestic news is fiscal and social — R88.6bn in unclaimed accounts and pensions, and a R1.34 a litre petrol rise on Tuesday despite a stronger rand.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: Two Brazilian stories sit behind the run to a series high: the collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe, which tested confidence in supervision, and a new poll showing the president's lead evaporating — a race markets read as open. The index reached 185,200 on Sep 2 after bottoming at 166,300 on Aug 18.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits below where it started the window, having fallen from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a Aug 18 low of 63,930 before recovering to 64,880. The feed carries no Mexican event explaining the decline.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits near the lower end of a 64-day range that peaked on Jul 22 and bottomed on Aug 19, down about 6 percent across the window. The input names no Argentine market event behind the move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has climbed through a trade fight with Washington. Canada vowed a 'dollar for dollar' response to US tariffs and refused relief on heavy trucks, then matched the tariffs on 25 August with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles; Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index has drifted up over the window despite the return of open conflict between the US and Iran: strikes resumed on 1 September after a month-long pause, Iran answered with missiles and drones, and a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Domestic legal news cut the other way — a judge ruled Google need not sell its ad exchange.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing through the summer, with the high on Jul 29 and the low back on Jun 9. Brent crude rose 3% to $90.97 on Iran strikes, lifting the energy names that anchor the index, while the London Stock Exchange set out plans for tokenized UK shares.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index slipped from its Aug 28 high as Germany formally blamed Russia for the attempted drone strike on a cargo aircraft at Leipzig Airport, then opened investigations into two substations hit with homemade explosives. Berlin is closing Russia's consulate in Bonn, and the EU summoned Moscow's envoy.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Paris-listed defence and space names have had a steady run of orders: Sweden signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates at €1.1 billion each, and the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three rocket startups. The index sits near 8,281 after peaking at 8,726 on Aug 10.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing about 5% over the summer, with the high on Aug 13 and the low on Jun 5. European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, a three-year high, with storage entering the winter at a record low.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run of roughly 8% over the window, with the Aug 11 high of 20,210 well above the Jun 10 low of 18,140. The most recent session eased 0.23% as protests spread across Spain over the government's handling of the Ceuta migrant crisis and Italy extended its Schengen border-check suspension with Spain to September 15.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its three-month range, but the coverage window explains little of the move directly. Global bonds have slumped to multi-year highs in yield, a selloff concentrated at the long end and driven by how much debt governments intend to issue — the transmission that matters most for a bank-heavy Milan listing.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index has climbed roughly eight percent across the window, from its June 3 low of 13,220 to a August 10 peak of 14,630, and sits near the top of that range at 14,360. Nothing in the available material accounts for the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index touched its 66-day high of 3331 on Aug 28, days before Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group at €1.1 billion each — an order placed abroad rather than with a domestic yard. It has since slipped 1.3% to 3266.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,057, down about 4% across the past 64 days from its 12 June high of 4,292 and near the 29 June low of 3,966. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the coming meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the case for a cut or a hike strengthens.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The no-change price has fallen from 75 on Aug 15 to 41 on Sep 2, sitting at 48 now, as an oil shock pushed the market from expecting a Fed cut to pricing a possible hike this month. Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes is an inflation shock, and Warsh said the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia biography of the sitting US president, and one of the most-read pages on the site. Daily readership rises whenever he acts, so the curve works as a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention American executive decisions are holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 26 August peak came as Washington's Saudi nuclear deal was found to skip an enrichment ban, and readership stayed high through a run of unilateral acts: a fake video of the Kharg Island oil terminal exploding, a request that regulators punish NBC anchor Kristen Welker, and a declaration that Hormuz was clear.

wiki-united-states.standing: The Wikipedia country article for the United States, and one of the most-read pages on the site. Its daily readership rises when Americans and readers abroad go looking for context on Washington's wars, elections and institutions.
wiki-united-states.recent: Readership climbed as US strikes on Iran resumed after a month's pause, with the low on Aug 22 giving way to the peak on Aug 28. A supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 31, the UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore the same day, and Iran said missiles struck Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan, which hosts US troops.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Bitcoin article on Wikipedia — a rough gauge of public curiosity rather than of price. Attention tends to arrive with the newcomers, so it rises when the asset reaches people who do not already own it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The peak on Aug 24 sat with a run of institutional and access stories: Rakbank Islamic opened Bitcoin trading inside its shariah-compliant platform after a shariah board cleared it, and BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million. Bitcoin then surged to $80,020, a move traders read as a short squeeze.

wiki-nepal.standing: Daily pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan state of about 30 million between India and China. Readership tracks disasters, politics and the trekking season, and it is a rough gauge of outside attention.
wiki-nepal.recent: Readership followed the flash floods along the Nepal-China border: the 27 August peak came a day after the first tolls landed, with 400 tourists missing, and rose again as a newly formed barrier lake threatened a second burst. The toll passed 5,000 by 31 August, with about 4,500 still missing.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve charges banks to lend to each other overnight, and the anchor for the price of dollar credit worldwide. Mortgages, corporate loans and emerging-market dollar debt all reprice off it.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed has cut from 5% in Sep 2024 to 3.75%, but the easing path has reversed: Brent near $95-97 on resumed Iran strikes turned an expected cut into a possible hike, with hike odds at two-in-three this week. An oil shock is an inflation shock, so the 10-year Treasury yield hit 4.81% rather than rallying.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays banks on money they park with it overnight. It is the floor under euro-area borrowing costs, and mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate all move off it.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate has come down by more than a third across the series, from 3.5% in September 2024 to 2.25% now, with the trough at 2% in June 2025. The input does not explain what drove the easing.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans who want work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates, and the one voters feel first.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, unchanged over the window and near the bottom of its recent range — down from the 4.5% high of November 2025, and just above the 4.0% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Attention here tracks the country's politics, economy and security as they reach a global audience.
wiki-nigeria.recent: The clearest recent driver is Uber's shutdown in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect on 2 September, ending more than a decade in Lagos and leaving contractor drivers with vehicle loans and no wind-down. Earlier in the window, Atiku's pledge to restore petrol subsidy and Tinubu's suspension of three permanent secretaries drew coverage.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a parliamentary majority since the 2000s, takes the largest bloc of seats in the next State Duma election. Traders price the outcome; the number is a bet, not a forecast.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Odds firmed from 64 on Aug 4 to a high of 75 on Aug 30 across a month in which the war dominated and Moscow faced no domestic challenge: Russia claimed it destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants, a strike near Kyiv killed 37, and Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone plot. Traders now hold it at 71.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iran by a set date. It is what traders will pay for de-escalation, so it falls when the shooting widens and rises when mediation looks real.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Odds collapsed as the war restarted rather than wound down: US strikes resumed on 1 September after a month-long pause, Iran answered with missiles at Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan, and Washington adopted a tanker-for-tanker targeting policy. Pakistan's mediation push is the only opening, and it has not stopped the strikes.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States mounts a ground invasion of Iran before 2027. It prices what traders will pay for that outcome, so it separates a shooting war fought from the air and sea from the far rarer step of putting troops on Iranian soil.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Strikes resumed on 1 September after a month-long pause, and Iran answered with missiles at Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan, yet the contract has drifted down from 22% on 4 August toward its 13% low on 28 August. The escalation has stayed at range — drones on tankers, a strike near Kuhestak, mines in the Strait of Hormuz — while Pakistan presses mediation.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel and Iran will have a ceasefire in place by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each strike, mediation attempt and pause in the fighting.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The month-long lull ended when US strikes resumed on 1 September and Iran answered with missiles and drones the same night, including a claimed hit on Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan, where US troops are hosted. A US drone strike on a wedding at Kuhestak killed five, and Pakistan says it remains "hopeful" of mediating between Tehran and Washington.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced in cents on the dollar. It is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as candidates enter, exit or falter.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract climbed from 26 on Aug 5 to 43 on Sep 3, its high for the window. The input carries nothing on the Brazilian race itself to explain the rise.

xag.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated physical silver, so it tracks the metal's spot price. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so it answers to investors and factories at once.
xag.recent: Silver ran from $50.58 on Aug 24 to $69.42 on Aug 28, better than a third in four days, and has since eased back to $65.79, leaving it up about 17% over the month. Nothing available accounts for the jump.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Crude oil and the fuels refined from it — the input behind transport, plastics, fertiliser and much of the world's electricity. Its price sets freight and food costs, and its supply is concentrated in a handful of exporting states and sea lanes.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Readership tracked a supply shock: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 after strikes on Iran, then two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz. Washington's move on Venezuela's reserves — 65 billion barrels, taken through a vehicle named North American Blue Energy Partners — kept the subject in view alongside Pakistan's Rs114 fuel levy.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A prediction market on who the Republican Party will nominate for president in 2028. Traders buy and sell shares that pay out if the named candidate wins the nomination, so the price is what people will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.recent: The contract climbed from 43% on Aug 8 to 53% on Sep 3, its highest of the window, with no news in this period bearing on the nomination itself. What moved around prediction markets was regulatory and legal: the Ninth Circuit ruled on Aug 28 that Kalshi's sports contracts aren't "swaps," and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A prediction market on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will hold the Israeli premiership after the next handover of power. It is a live read on the durability of a coalition that has governed through war, prosecution and repeated crises.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The price drifted down through August as Netanyahu absorbed pressure abroad and at home: Turkey moved to seek an Interpol notice over the Gaza flotilla case, European powers rebuked Israel over the E1 settlement plan, and the war ground on. It bottomed at 25% on Aug 28, then recovered after he told Gaza troops "we are not retreating.

poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marine Le Pen becomes president of France in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on candidacy rulings, coalition arithmetic and polling rather than on any single campaign event.
poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.recent: The contract has drifted up from 30% on Aug 4 to 36% on Sep 3, its high for the month. Nothing in the window explains the move; the Polymarket stories here concern the platform itself, including 152 wallets showing a 97.2% win rate on war markets.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic holds the best AI model when the market settles. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it tracks how crowded the bet on a single lab's lead at the frontier has become.
poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.recent: The contract traded in a wide band over the month, bottoming at 78 on Aug 11, peaking at 94 on Aug 31, and sitting at 87 now. Nothing in the window accounts for the swing.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance becomes the next US president. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it is a live read on how the field around a sitting vice-president is being priced rather than a poll of voters.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The contract drifted up from 20% on Aug 21 to 25% on Aug 30, a move that ran alongside scrutiny of the prediction markets themselves rather than any campaign news: the Ninth Circuit ruled Kalshi's sports bets aren't "swaps," and a White House aide paid a fine over bets placed on Trump's speeches.

poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrat leader and a former Swedish prime minister, takes the office next. The price is what traders will pay for a yes — money backing an outcome, not a forecast of it.
poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.recent: The price has slid from 93 on Aug 24, its high for the month, to 80 on Sep 3 — a steady drift rather than a single break. Nothing in the past month's news accounts for the move.

poly-will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI ships its next flagship model by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on release signals rather than on any official schedule.
poly-will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september.recent: The contract ran from 20% on Aug 28 to 90% on Sep 3, a jump that the available material does not explain — the surrounding prediction-market news concerns regulation and trading conduct, not model releases: a Ninth Circuit ruling on Aug 28 that state authorities may treat Kalshi's sports contracts as bets rather than swaps, and a $65,000 insider-trading settlement by a White House teleprompter operator on Aug 29.

poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Josh Shapiro becomes the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on primary field news rather than on polling alone.
poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The contract has sat flat at 5% across the past month, with no movement to explain. What news there was concerned the venues rather than the field: the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets are not "swaps", confirming state powers over prediction markets, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he had read early.

wiki-economic-sanctions.standing: Restrictions one state places on another's trade, finance or individuals, used as leverage short of war. They work through banks and shipping, so their reach depends on whether third countries and their lenders choose to comply.
wiki-economic-sanctions.recent: Readership tracked Washington's Iran campaign: the 24 August peak came as Treasury Secretary Bessent named the programme "Economic Outcast" and Treasury designated nearly 60 entities, the same day the rial opened at a record 2.02 million per dollar. Tehran has since admitted foreign trade shrank by more than a third.

stocks:GOOG.standing: Alphabet is the holding company behind Google — search, YouTube, Android and Google Cloud — and one of the largest firms by market value. Its shares are a proxy for the advertising market and for how investors price the returns on AI spending.
stocks:GOOG.recent: The stock fell about a tenth over the past month, from 375.40 on Aug 4 to a low of 332 on Sep 1. Google's move to price a cybersecurity model per token, announced from Mountain View on Sep 2, points to where the company is pushing its AI products, but the input does not explain the slide.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the world's largest consumer-electronics company, whose revenue still rests mostly on the iPhone. Its results move component suppliers across Asia, and its weight in the major US indices means a move in the stock drags them with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple confirmed a September 9 event for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and on Tuesday John Ternus took over as CEO from Tim Cook. Enterprise AI buyers emptied Mac inventory, a demand shock Apple had misjudged. The stock's high on Sep 1 followed the succession announcement.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Avigdor Lieberman, the secular-right Yisrael Beiteinu leader and former Israeli defence and foreign minister, becomes Israel's next prime minister. It prices how traders rate an opposition figure's odds of taking the top job.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The contract drifted up from 4% on Aug 4 to 7% on Sep 3 as Netanyahu, visiting Gaza, said "we are not retreating" and Gaza's health ministry put the toll since October's ceasefire at 1,334. Turkey moved to seek an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case, and European powers rebuked Israel over the West Bank E1 settlement plan.

poly-will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI releases a model called GPT-6 by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it moves on hiring leaks, benchmark rumours and launch-event scheduling rather than on any announcement itself.
poly-will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september.recent: The contract went from 9% on Aug 26 to 87%, an almost complete repricing inside a week, and the input carries nothing that explains it — the surrounding stories are about the venues rather than the question, with the Ninth Circuit ruling on Aug 28 that sports bets aren't "swaps" and a White House aide fined on Aug 29 over speech bets.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by year-end. The strait carries a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, so the price is a running read on how long traders think the disruption lasts.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders have halved the odds since early August as the US-Iran exchange widened: two Iranian tankers were struck by US drones, a supertanker hit mines in the strait, and Iran now says transit requires Tehran's permission. Some 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships, and Brent rose 3% to $90.97.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel shuts its airspace to civil aviation before a set date. Traders price it as a proxy for the risk of a wider regional war, since closures follow missile exchanges and mass-casualty escalation rather than the grinding daily violence.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's leader before the end of 2026. Traders are pricing the odds of a leadership change in a nuclear-armed state that runs a war economy, so the number is a bet, not a forecast.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The price has drifted down to 7% over the past month, from a high of 9% on Aug 4. Nothing in the war has touched Putin's position: Germany formally blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig airport, Norway detained the research vessel Professor Molchanov at Barentsburg on a Naftogaz arbitral award, and the Shanghai bloc in Bishkek declined to name Ukraine at all.

wiki-flood.standing: The number of people reading Wikipedia's article on floods each day. It rises when water is the story somewhere — a burst river, a cloudburst, a lake that gives way — and is a rough gauge of how widely a disaster has registered.
wiki-flood.recent: Reading followed the Himalayan flood disaster: a flash flood near the Nepal-China border on 26 August left hundreds missing, and by 1 September the toll had passed 1,000, then 5,000, with nearly 12,000 rescued. The 28 August peak also caught the Grand Canyon flash flood, where a Texas chiropractor died and 15 were missing.

stocks:META.standing: Shares in the company that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, whose revenue comes almost entirely from advertising sold against that attention. It is one of the largest US-listed technology firms, so its price moves index funds and the wider market with it.
stocks:META.recent: The stock fell to 543.7 on Aug 18 and recovered through late August, spanning the $17.1bn settlement over social media harms to children announced on Aug 26 — roughly 1% of Meta's stock value, and a deal whose product changes rewrite defaults worldwide. Meta also scrapped plans to go "AI native" by slashing some teams by 60 percent.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at the meeting after September. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the case for tightening strengthens or weakens.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes turned an expected cut into a possible hike, pushing the contract from 25% on Aug 15 to a 59% peak on Sep 2. An oil shock is an inflation shock, and a central bank with one instrument cannot separate a tanker strike from domestic demand. It sits at 51% as shares and bonds rally awaiting Fed signals.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve holds its policy rate flat through the year. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, so it moves with every signal about where the central bank thinks inflation is going.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes turned the question from when the Fed cuts to whether it hikes, with hike odds reaching two-in-three this week; Warsh said the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade. An oil shock is an inflation shock, and a central bank with one instrument must answer it.

wiki-vladimir-putin.standing: Russia's president since 2000, aside from a term as prime minister, and the single decision-maker behind its wars, energy policy and foreign alignments. What he says on a given day moves oil, currencies and NATO planning.
wiki-vladimir-putin.recent: The rise tracks a week of summitry: Putin met Modi and Xi at the SCO gathering in Bishkek, one of nine bilateral meetings, where Modi urged dialogue over battlefield solutions while continuing to buy Russian crude. Putin also sparred publicly with Pashinyan, warning Armenia it cannot join two customs unions at once.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on who wins the Democratic presidential nomination in 2028, priced as what traders will pay for a Newsom win. It is a bet on a party contest, not a poll, and it reprices on anything that changes a candidate's standing.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The month's drift down came alongside a run of bad news for prediction markets themselves rather than for Newsom: the Ninth Circuit ruled on 28 August that Kalshi's sports contracts aren't "swaps", handing states regulatory power, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Édouard Philippe becomes France's next president in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the shape of the field — who enters, who withdraws, who is disqualified.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: The contract drifted from 25% on Aug 24 to 28% on Sep 2, a move with no French political event behind it in the material available. The Polymarket news of the window was about the venue rather than the race: a fined White House aide who bet on speeches, a Ninth Circuit ruling curbing Kalshi, and 152 wallets showing a 97.2% win rate on war odds.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A prediction market on whether the Clarity Act, a US crypto market-structure bill, becomes law during 2026. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it tracks how passable the bill looks to people with money on it.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The slide ran alongside a bad month for the prediction-market industry itself: on 28 August the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts aren't "swaps", confirming state powers over prediction markets, and Connecticut filed its own suit the day before. A day later a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine to settle an insider-trading case over bets on Trump's speeches.

poly-will-openai-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI will hold the strongest publicly available AI model when the market settles. It prices a lab's standing against its rivals, and traders move it when a competitor ships.
poly-will-openai-have-the-best-ai-model-.recent: The contract sat near its 32-day low of 3% on Aug 17 before recovering to 11%, a move the input does not explain. Polymarket itself was the news: 152 wallets showed a 97.2% win rate on war outcomes, a White House aide paid a fine over bets on the president's speeches, and the Ninth Circuit ruled against Kalshi.

wiki-venezuela.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Venezuela each day. It rises when the country enters a story big enough to send readers looking for the background — the oil, the politics, the map.
wiki-venezuela.recent: Readership tracked the handover of Venezuela's oil: the 29 August peak came as 65 billion barrels changed hands in Caracas, and readers returned through the weekend as Maduro posted photos from a Brooklyn cell and Trump said Exxon was 'going in' after 19 years out. María Corina Machado has since contested who had standing to sign.

stocks:CVX.standing: One of the largest US oil majors, an integrated producer and refiner whose share price tracks crude and the fortunes of the fields it is allowed to operate. Where it holds licences is a political question as much as a commercial one.
stocks:CVX.recent: The stock's run to its high came with Venezuela: Bloomberg reported on 1 September that Chevron was nearing a deal to run two fields in the Orinoco Belt, and 65 billion barrels are now under contract. María Corina Machado faulted the terms on 3 September while backing the US partnership.

stocks:BLK.standing: The world's largest asset manager, running trillions of dollars in index funds, ETFs and pensions on behalf of institutions and retail savers. Where it opens a product or a market, other money follows.
stocks:BLK.recent: The stock drifted down through late August to a low of $1,107 on Sep 2, against a high of $1,183 on Aug 13. The distribution story ran alongside it: BlackRock cut the swap-in threshold on its bitcoin product from $25 million to $1 million on Aug 26, and Bitget's CEO said BlackRock and other Wall Street firms are seeking expansion in Asian markets, where half of the exchange's 125 million users sit.

stocks:FMCC.standing: Freddie Mac, the government-sponsored enterprise that buys mortgages from US lenders, packages them into securities and guarantees the payments. Its shares track investor views on the American housing-finance system it underwrites.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The listed shares of the company whose graphics processors train and run most of the world's large AI models. Its order book is the closest thing to a meter on AI capital spending, and chipmakers, data-centre builders and power utilities all read off it.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The run followed a fortnight of Nvidia extending itself across the whole AI stack: it guided to $108bn in revenue next quarter, pledged $500 billion to its own buyers and backstopped $230 billion in customer lease obligations, then agreed to buy Hugging Face above $13 billion and took a $3.5 billion convertible stake option in MediaTek.
